doc.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Herman Leonard, the photographer, and the Short Cuts quarrel
summary: She knew Leonard from Paris; a letter over unauthorized use of his portraits in Short Cuts cooled their friendship, and they talk about his archive after Katrina.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah. Herman I knew from Paris. He was very sweet. He was the toast of Paris. He took one – that’s his, right there. We were friends until I did Short Cuts. Bob’s – Bob Altman’s son was the set designer. He had gone around, and he’s gotten all these wonderful Herman Leonard portraits. He didn’t ask permission. Herman wrote a letter to Bob. It was scathing. It really was not deserved. He accused Bob of being anti-feminine in his approach in movies. It was an awful letter. He – I think they had to pay him a certain amount for permission, because it had already been filmed. After that, I didn’t keep as close touch with Herman as I had been in the past. He was a master. He was a wonderful photographer.
Do you see any in action in Birdland when he was photographing? Do you remember anything about . . . ?
No. I never saw him photograph. He had a studio in that lake. Is it Pontchartrain?
Yeah. He had a whole collection there, which apparently he saved during Katrina.
Anyway, he ended up having to move. He moved back to Los Angeles.
Because he actually lost some of his collection.
